newsitem.title: USA: CBOT Jan soybeans near three-month highs on stocks.
newsitem.headline: CBOT Jan soybeans near three-month highs on stocks.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures rallied early Monday on follow through from Friday's bullish USDA crop production and ending stocks reports, with January hitting its highest point in three months, traders said.
"It's following through plus South America is heating up," a trader said.

The January contract touched $7.34-1/2 per bushel as of 1035 CST, just below the $7.35 reached during Friday's bull move. Monday morning's high was near the three-month high which was set when January traded at $7.37 on October 11.

USDA on Friday estimated 1996 U.S. soybean production at 2.382 billion bushels, below average expectations for 2.407 billion. USDA also said the 1996-97 U.S. soy carryover would total 155 million bushels, below the previous forecast for 180 million bushels. Traders said there was a private outlook for soybean ending stocks to total 140 million bushels.
Support came from concern about hot weather in Brazil. Brazilian growers said some areas in Rio Grande do Sul remained without rain and were starting to suffer losses.
But soy gains were limited by increased farmer selling.
At 1042 CST, soybeans were two to 9-1/4 cents per bushel higher, with January up 6-1/4 at $7.33.
Traders said the market was again buoyed by speculative buying while commercial selling Friday and again Monday, tied to farmer selling, limited rallies.
In early dealings on Monday, Rosenthal Collins bought one million bushels of March and Cargill Inc bought one million bushels of July, they said.
But traders said a lighter-than-expected soybean export inspections number also limited advances in the January contract, the traders said.
USDA Monday said 20.998 million bushels of U.S. soybeans were inspected for export during the week ended January 9, below expectations for 24 million to 28 million bushels.
